label: last two copy-phase steps (end of output)
explanation: Almost entirely a copy-phase feature (99.7% of activation mass), concentrated at the end of the copy. to_go == 0 (final output) holds 66% of the mass, to_go <= 1 holds 82%, and to_go <= 3 holds 99%. It never fires in the original phase (except a trace at t = 5-6 on repeated tokens) and never at the delimiter or in sequences with L = 3. Firing also depends on absolute step: the rate peaks at t = 13-15 (0.21-0.38). For L = 9 the peak comes 3-4 steps before the end (t = 13-14), not at the last step, and for L = 4 the feature fires at the final step t = 7. Precision is low (about 0.24): within the late-copy window it fires on only a subset of sequences, and no token-content variable separated those well. The output tokens w, a, k, q and m raise the rate about 1.5x, and many digits in the sequence lower it slightly, but conditioning on these did not improve F1. Magnitude is not clearly modulated by any single variable checked; the strongest examples are mid-to-late copy steps in L = 8-9 sequences.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the previous input (most: c, q, a, n, f, w; least: k, h, r, <DEL>) and the token being output, by phase (delimiter step: c, q, 0, w; copy phase: w, a, k, q; input phase: ); timing cues that raise it most: L=4 & t=7, to_go=0, recall_idx=5.
